title: What If You Relived One Race Until You Beat Michael Phelps?
description:
What if you relived one race until you beat Michael Phelps?

Beijing, 2008. The 100m butterfly final, won by the smallest margin a swimming clock can measure. You're in lane zero, the empty lane they leave for the waves, and every time you lose, you're back on the block. Your body resets. Your technique doesn't.

56.0. 54.6. 53.0. 51.1. Then a wall at 50.62. Then a discovery about the last five meters that decided an Olympic final.

Real facts inside: the 10-lane Water Cube, Phelps seventh at the turn, the half-stroke finish, and the touchpad that needs a push, not a touch.

GLIDE or SMASH? Comment below.

title: ¿Y si los humanos NUNCA hubieran inventado la ropa?
description:
¿Y si la ropa nunca se hubiera inventado? Sin abrigo, nadie habría cruzado el frío, y América se habría quedado vacía. Ni tú, ni tu ciudad, ni este idioma existirían. Subimos piso por piso para ver cómo sería ese mundo: el frío, el sol, los pies descalzos, los mosquitos… y quién inventaría la primera prenda.

Capítulos:
0:00 Un continente vacío
0:32 Piso 1: El frío
1:27 Piso 2: El sol
1:55 Piso 3: Los pies
2:21 Piso 4: Los bichos
2:43 Piso 5: ¿Cuántos seríamos?
3:04 Piso 6: La primera prenda
3:33 Salida

Fuentes:
- Origen de la ropa (genética de los piojos de la ropa, hace 83.000-170.000 años): Toups et al., 2011, Molecular Biology and Evolution.
- Zona termoneutral del cuerpo desnudo (~27 °C) y temblor (hasta ~5 veces el gasto en reposo): Haman, 2006.
- Temperatura media de la Tierra: ~15 °C (NASA / NOAA).
- Poblamiento de América por Beringia (hace ~15.000-20.000 años).
- Piel oscura y melanina como protección solar: Jablonski y Chaplin, 2000; Rogers et al., 2004.
- Quemadura solar en menos de 15 minutos con índice UV alto: OMS / EPA.
- Temperatura del asfalto bajo el sol (más de 60 °C): Vanos et al., 2016.
- Callos que protegen sin quitar sensibilidad: Holowka et al., 2019, Nature.
- Malaria (~600.000 muertes al año): OMS, World Malaria Report.
- ~40 % de la población mundial vive en los trópicos: State of the Tropics Report, 2014. La cifra de 3 mil millones es una estimación para esta historia alternativa.
- Domesticación del algodón (hace ~7.000 años).

#QuéPasaríaSi #Historia #Ciencia

title: What If You Could See Everyone's Luck
description:
What If You Could See Everyone's Luck?

What if you could see everyone's luck? You wake up one morning and there's a number floating over your head: three percent. Your little sister, who has never lost a game of Uno in her life, is at ninety-two. Your mum, five months out of work, is at two. And the old man at the bus stop, who in the last ten seconds has been hit by a pigeon, dropped his phone in a puddle and watched his bus drive away without him, is at ninety-nine.

At first it's amazing. Your luck is three percent, but nobody said your luck had to be the luck that counts. So for one week, your sister makes every choice you have. She picks the canteen queue, the last slice of pizza, the only bus that isn't cancelled, and the answers to a quiz you didn't study for. Then she reaches into the school raffle jar and pulls out your ticket. First prize: a games console. Then she loses a game of Uno, and her number starts to drop.

Every win you had that week was paid for by somebody. And a box at the top of your mum's wardrobe is about to tell you why your own number has been stuck at three for eleven years.

Would you spend your luck, or save it? Tell us in the comments.

#whatif #animation #luck

title: What IF the Nerd Dated the Most Popular Girl in School?
description:
What if the nerd dated the most popular girl in school? 💘📚 You’re used to being noticed for your exam scores—not your love life. Then the most popular girl in school asks you out, and suddenly everyone has an opinion. Could you enjoy your first date without worrying about what the whole school thinks?

In this animated what-if story, we imagine an unexpected relationship between two people everyone assumed had nothing in common. From awkward lunch-table introductions to discovering shared interests, getting to know each other means looking past the labels your classmates gave you.

Would you try to fit into her social circle or feel comfortable introducing her to yours? Friends might jump to conclusions, rumours could turn ordinary moments into drama, and both of you could feel pressure to act differently. What happens when you disagree—and everyone treats it like school-wide news?

This school romance explores confidence, friendship, and the surprise of connecting with someone beyond their reputation. Could you build a relationship on being yourselves—or let other people’s expectations get in the way?
